issues.description: `is_partition` places pairwise disjointness and full-union coverage inside a per-part implication, so an empty `parts` set vacuously partitions every set, including a non-empty `s`.
issues.rationale: For `parts = Set::<Set<A>>::empty()`, the antecedent `parts.contains(part)` is false for every `part`; therefore the entire `forall` is true without evaluating the nested `pairwise_disjoint(parts)` or `s == parts.flatten()` conjuncts. The old predicate consequently returns true for any `s`, although the union of an empty family is empty. The PR body gives exactly this counterexample, the maintainer explicitly thanks the author for identifying the bug, and the one-commit fix moves the two family-wide conditions outside the quantifier and adds a lemma proving that empty parts partition exactly an empty set.
issues.source_evidence:
before/verified_libs/vstd_extra/src/set_extra.rs
154: pub open spec fn is_partition<A>(s: Set<A>, parts: Set<Set<A>>) -> bool {
156:     forall|part: Set<A>| #[trigger]
157:         parts.contains(part) ==> !part.is_empty() && part <= s
158:             &&
159:         // Parts are pairwise disjoint
160:         pairwise_disjoint(parts) &&
161:         // Union of parts is s
162:         s == parts.flatten()
163: }

With `parts` empty, line 157's implication is true for every `part`, so lines 160-162 do not constrain `s`. The after version moves lines 160-162 outside the `forall` and adds `lemma_is_partition_empty_parts`, whose ensures states `is_partition(s, empty) == s.is_empty()`.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus was not re-executed. Read the complete archived and current remote discussion, checked the official base/head Git objects and true merge-base, instantiated the empty-parts counterexample in the fixed before source, and confirmed the after predicate plus its new boundary lemma remove the vacuous case.
